title: Urine–serum concentration interaction did not establish added albuminuria prediction across NHANES waves
abstract: A prespecified interaction between measured urine osmolality and calculated serum osmolarity was tested for added single-spot albuminuria prediction. Models trained in 4,593 NHANES2009–10 adults were frozen and applied to3,960 NHANES2011–12 adults. Beyond flexible marginal laboratory and conventional risk-factor terms, the interaction changed weighted target Brier score by -0.00015182; a target-only stratified PSU bootstrap interval was [-0.00033436,0.00003256] and a two-wave full-refit interval was [-0.00074946,0.00077299]. Source grouped cross-validation worsened. Thus the prespecified criterion failed despite a small favorable target point estimate. Separate survey waves are not an independent clinical program. Findings do not establish a biomarker, renal concentrating defect, or absence of all useful interaction information.
